chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was martyred, and upon him was a dark-colored coat of khazz, and they found therein sixty-three [wounds], from among strikes with the sword, stabbings with the spear, or shootings with the arrow.

key_terms.جُبَّة: A loose outer garment, coat or robe worn as outerwear in classical Islamic society
key_terms.خَزّ: Khazz: a mixed silk-wool fabric that was considered permissible to wear in Shia jurisprudence, contrasting with pure silk which is forbidden for men
key_terms.دَكْنَاء: Dark-colored; referring to the deep hue of the garment, which made the wounds visible

ai.seo_question: How many wounds did Imam Husayn receive at the Battle of Karbala?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates that when Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was martyred at Karbala on the Day of Ashura (10 Muharram 61 AH), his body bore sixty-three wounds inflicted by swords, spears, and arrows. This account specifically notes that his garment — a dark coat of khazz fabric — bore visible evidence of every blow. The narration is transmitted through Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, a trusted companion of Imam al-Baqir, and serves to document the extent of the martyrdom's brutality.
